title: Car Grip
description: A car mount camera bolts to hood, door, or bumper so bodywork sits in the near plane and asphalt slides underneath. Chrome and road share one rigid relationship because the rig is the machine.

sections.title: Narrative function

blocks.text: Bolt the camera to the machine. Product, chase punctuation, a car as the hero: we are glued to this one body, dirt on the lens allowed.
A tracking shot from another car that never sees this car's body is not grip. Buckle-up is inside; grip is the metal.

sections.title: What usually goes wrong

blocks.text: The usual wrong cousin is a tracking shot from another vehicle with no bodywork in frame. The tell: a clean three-quarter of a car, camera floating.
The fix: bolt to this car, keep metal in the near plane, let the road slide.

sections.title: Questions

blocks.text: What is Car Grip in film?
Car grip is a camera bolted to the vehicle's bodywork. Hood, door, or bumper stays in the near plane while the road slides underneath.
Car Grip vs Buckle Up
Buckle up is inside the cabin with the people. Car grip is outside on the metal, chrome and asphalt in one plane.
When should I use Car Grip?
Use it when the machine is the subject or a chase needs a body-mounted beat. Do not use it for a cabin dialogue.
How do I prompt Car Grip for AI image or video?
Write a mount on hood or door with bodywork in frame. Example: Car-grip mount on [Subject]'s vehicle, hood or door as the rig, chrome and asphalt in one plane.
